definition: Measuring the two failure surfaces separately: retrieval quality (did the right evidence arrive: context precision/recall, hit rate, MRR/nDCG) and generation quality (is the answer supported by the evidence: faithfulness/groundedness, answer relevance).
details: Measuring the two failure surfaces separately: retrieval quality (did the right evidence arrive: context precision/recall, hit rate, MRR/nDCG) and generation quality (is the answer supported by the evidence: faithfulness/groundedness, answer relevance). Frameworks like RAGAS operationalize these with LLM judges.

explainer.lead: RAG evaluation separates retrieval quality from generation quality: whether the right evidence arrived, and whether the answer is supported by that evidence. It matters because it isolates which of the two failure surfaces is causing bad answers.

tiers.eli5: It checks two things separately: did we fetch the right pages, and did the answer actually stick to what those pages said?
tiers.practitioner: Engineers track retrieval metrics such as context precision, recall, hit rate, MRR and nDCG alongside faithfulness, groundedness and answer relevance. A pitfall is conflating the two surfaces, so a retrieval failure is misread as a generation failure.
tiers.paperLevel: Retrieval quality is measured with context precision/recall, hit rate, MRR and nDCG; generation quality with faithfulness/groundedness and answer relevance. Frameworks like RAGAS operationalize these with LLM judges.

explainer.example: A system retrieves the correct document but the answer adds unsupported claims, so context precision passes while faithfulness fails.
